blocking_findings: Claim S-N3 relies on an equivocation of the composition operator. To test if limits commute with composition, the same interaction data (\kappa) must be supplied to both \lim_{\omega\to0}(\Sigma^{(1)}_\omega \otimes_\kappa \Sigma^{(2)}_\omega) and (\lim_{\omega\to0}\Sigma^{(1)}_\omega) \otimes_\kappa (\lim_{\omega\to0}\Sigma^{(2)}_\omega). Using \otimes_\kappa on the left but \otimes_0 on the right (justified by 'the factors determine none') creates an artificial non-commutation that trivially reflects \kappa \neq 0. If \kappa is preserved, the limits commute exactly.

Claim S-P1 asserts that the translation \tau maps the four layers of CS-N1 to pairwise distinct components of the tuple \mathcal{R} = (K,D,I,E,P,A). However, Table 2 maps both 'kinematical product' (layer 1) and 'observable embedding' (layer 2) to K. Since K is a single component of the 6-tuple, the mapping is not to pairwise distinct components.

counterexamples: Counterexample to S-N3: Supply the interaction data \kappa to the composition of the limits. The composite of the \omega\to0 limits of the isolated factors with interaction \kappa is H = p_1^2/2m + p_2^2/2m + \kappa q_1 q_2. This exactly matches the \omega\to0 limit of the composite, showing that the limit does commute with composition when the composition operator (\otimes_\kappa) is applied consistently.
